tasks.short: Review recordings and rehearsals against broadcast standards.

steps.what: Read the production and broadcast standards
Read mail that cites the booked length
Read the running time stored for this recording
Review recordings and rehearsals in the viewing room
Decide conformance to the broadcast production standards

tasks.design: The producer reads the production and broadcast standards in {DOCS}, the mail that cites the booked length in {EMAIL}, and the running time on {PROJECT}. In the viewing room the producer reviews the recordings and rehearsals and decides conformance. A scheduler that builds playlists from rights and repeat rules was weighed and left unused, because this task judges a take, and no standards list is maintained.
tasks.previous_blocker: Conformance depends on watching the take, and the standards do not decide a performance by themselves.
tasks.enabler_now: The running time is already stored on {PROJECT}, but that figure still does not judge the take, so nothing new is built.
tasks.still_hard: Seeing whether a rehearsal meets the broadcast standards.
tasks.human_edge: The producer hears tone, pace and whether the take is fit to broadcast.
tasks.altitude: The week still includes the viewing room. The producer keeps the conformance call.

reach.task: Assemble a cut to the booked programme length
reach.learn: Which defects the editor already removed before the producer watches the take

evidence.claim: Watching a recording or rehearsal and judging it against production standards is a person's judgement. A stored running time does not make that judgement.
Mediagenix Scheduling Automation checks rights, repeat limits and content rules when it builds playlists. That is channel programming, not a review of one take, so it is not used here.

assumptions: Means for this task are screens 3.5, spreadsheets 0.6, mail 2.4, documents 11.4 and meetings 82.1, which sum to 100. Largest remainder gives screens 4, spreadsheets 1, mail 2, documents 11 and meetings 82. The spreadsheet point is folded onto documents, so the steps use screens 4, mail 2, documents 12 and meetings 82. No spreadsheet is used.
No standards list, mapping or template is maintained. The standards are read as they stand in {DOCS}.
No machine step needs a structured input. The fallback for every read is the same human read of the standards, the mail and the running time.
The workflow boundary is this review of one recording or rehearsal. Channel scheduling, quota reports and the edit of the cut are other tasks and are not counted.
Watching and the conformance decision stay at full time because no mechanism shortens those steps. The running-time read is a real read of the stored duration.
unknowns: Whether a rehearsal that is not broadcast is judged against the same written standards as a transmission.
research_questions: Which written standards does this desk apply to a rehearsal that is not broadcast?

incremental.description: No separate standards list is maintained, so upkeep is zero.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: No step is shortened. The standards read, the length read, the viewing and the conformance call all stay with the producer, so low and high are both 0.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Study scripts and decide how they should be directed.

steps.what: Study scripts to determine how they should be directed
Read research kept with the scripts
Read mail that adds research on the scripts
Read the prior staging note for these scripts
Determine how these scripts should be directed

tasks.design: The producer studies the scripts in {DOCS}, reads the research kept with them and the mail in {EMAIL}, and reads the prior staging note on {PROJECT}. The producer then determines how these scripts should be directed. A production tool that drafts a scene breakdown was weighed and left unused, because the producer still chooses the direction, and no breakdown list is maintained.
tasks.previous_blocker: How a script should be directed is not a rule that covers the pages.
tasks.enabler_now: A production tool can draft scene elements, but the direction choice is still the producer's, so that draft is not built.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing the staging from an unstructured script.
tasks.human_edge: The producer decides what the scene is for.
tasks.altitude: The week still includes the scripts. The producer keeps the direction choice.

reach.task: Discuss the first assembly with the director
reach.learn: Which direction choices the editor still needs stated in words

evidence.claim: Choosing how a script should be directed is the producer's judgement. A list of scenes does not choose the staging.

Yamdu offers an AI script breakdown in beta since October 2025. The producer would still confirm each element, and this design does not build that loop, because the direction choice stays with the person.

assumptions: Means are screens 1.8, spreadsheets 1.4, mail 5.9, documents 47.0 and meetings 44.0, which sum to 100.1. The 0.1 overage is stated. Scaling by 100/100.1 and taking the largest remainder, and the unscaled largest remainder, both publish screens 2, spreadsheets 1, mail 6, documents 47 and meetings 44. The spreadsheet point is folded onto documents, so the steps use screens 2, mail 6, documents 48 and meetings 44. No spreadsheet is used.
No script breakdown list, mapping or template is maintained.
No machine step needs a structured input. The fallback is the producer reading the scripts and the research.
The workflow boundary is how these scripts should be directed. Casting, composing and publishing a cut are other tasks and are not counted.
A production tool that drafts scene elements was weighed. The direction decision stays at full time because a scene list would not choose the staging.
unknowns: Whether the direction is spoken only, or also written down after the study.
research_questions: Who else, if anyone, must accept the direction before rehearsal starts?

incremental.description: No script breakdown list is maintained, so upkeep is zero.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: No step is shortened. Studying the scripts, the research and the direction choice all stay with the producer, so low and high are both 0.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Supervise and coordinate camera, lighting, design and sound crew.

steps.what: Read the crew plan for camera, lighting, design and sound
Read mail from crew about camera and sound
Read stored positions for lighting and camera
Supervise camera, lighting, design and sound crew members
Coordinate the next setup with those crew members

tasks.design: The producer reads the crew plan in {DOCS}, mail from the crew in {EMAIL}, and the stored lighting and camera positions on {PROJECT}. On the floor the producer supervises the camera, lighting, design and sound crew and coordinates the next setup. A prepared crew list from a production tool was weighed and left unused, because the supervision is live and no crew map is maintained.
tasks.previous_blocker: The next setup changes with what just happened on the floor.
tasks.enabler_now: A production tool can prepare a crew list, but the list does not direct the crew, so it is not used.
tasks.still_hard: Calling the next move for camera, lighting, design and sound while they work.
tasks.human_edge: The producer sees the room and the people in it.
tasks.altitude: The week still includes the floor. The producer keeps the calls to the crew.

reach.role: Camera Operators, Television, Video, and Film
reach.task: Operate a camera during a rehearsal
reach.learn: Which camera positions the operator can change without a new call

evidence.claim: Supervising camera, lighting, design and sound crew on the floor is situational coordination. A prepared crew list does not direct the next setup.
Yamdu prepares call sheets and schedules. A call sheet is not the supervision, so that feature is not used for this task.

assumptions: Means are screens 2.3, spreadsheets 2.3, mail 8.7, documents 9.6 and meetings 77.1, which sum to 100. Floors are 2, 2, 8, 9 and 77. The two remainder points go to mail 0.7 and documents 0.6, so the published split is screens 2, spreadsheets 2, mail 9, documents 10 and meetings 77. The spreadsheet points are folded onto documents, so the steps use screens 2, mail 9, documents 12 and meetings 77. No spreadsheet is used.
No crew map, mapping or template is maintained.
No machine step needs a structured input. The fallback is the producer reading the crew plan, the mail and the stored positions.

The workflow boundary is supervision of camera, lighting, design and sound crew on this production. Hiring, payroll and channel scheduling are other tasks and are not counted. Crew talk stays inside the organisation.
A prepared crew list was weighed and left unused. The floor supervision stays at full time.
unknowns: How many of the camera, lighting, design and sound crew are employees of this company.
research_questions: Which crew roles are employees, and which are hired for the production?

incremental.description: No crew map is maintained, so upkeep is zero.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: No step is shortened. Reading the plan and supervising the crew both stay with the producer, so low and high are both 0.

tasks.short: Confer on photography, script, music, sets and costumes.

steps.what: Read notes on photography, script, music and costumes
Read mail about production details before the confer
Read stored notes on sets and costumes
Confer with technical directors, managers and writers
Discuss production details with crew members

tasks.design: The producer reads notes on photography, script, music and costumes in {DOCS}, mail about the production details in {EMAIL}, and the stored notes on {PROJECT}. The producer then confers with technical directors, managers, writers and crew members and discusses those details in the room. A scene breakdown does not hold that talk, and no costume list is maintained.
tasks.previous_blocker: The details are settled by people talking, not by a form.
tasks.enabler_now: Notes and mail already exist to read beforehand. They do not replace the conference, so nothing is built.
tasks.still_hard: Getting directors, managers, writers and crew to one agreed detail.
tasks.human_edge: The producer hears disagreement and chooses in the room.
tasks.altitude: The week still includes the conference. The producer keeps the discussion.

reach.task: Set the technical plan for photography and sound
reach.learn: Which technical details are already settled before the conference

evidence.claim: Conferring with technical directors, managers, writers and crew about photography, script, music and costumes is live talk. A stored note does not hold the discussion.
Yamdu's script breakdown drafts scene elements a producer confirms. It does not confer with writers or crew, so it does not shorten this meeting.

assumptions: Means are screens 1.1, spreadsheets 0.8, mail 9.9, documents 11.7 and meetings 76.4, which sum to 99.9. The 0.1 shortfall is stated. Scaling by 100/99.9 and taking the largest remainder publishes screens 1, spreadsheets 1, mail 10, documents 12 and meetings 76. The spreadsheet point is folded onto documents, so the steps use screens 1, mail 10, documents 13 and meetings 76. No spreadsheet is used.
No costume list, mapping or template is maintained.
No machine step needs a structured input. The fallback is the producer reading the notes and the mail before the meeting.
The workflow boundary is this conference. Writing the script, composing the music and designing the costumes are other tasks and are not counted. The people in the room are colleagues.
The conference stays at full time. A stored note does not hold the discussion.
unknowns: Whether photography, music and costume details are settled only in the room.
research_questions: Does the technical director have to accept a written detail, or is the spoken conference enough?

incremental.description: No costume or set list is maintained, so upkeep is zero.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: No step is shortened. The notes, the mail and the conference all stay with the producer, so low and high are both 0.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
